entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Martin Luther?
entries.text: Martin Luther (November 10, 1483 ‒ February 18, 1546) was a German monk and theologian of Christianity credited with leading the Protestant Reformation, a movement that marked the start of Protestantism. Luther founded the Lutheran Church, the first large Protestant church.
entries.title: Martin Luther

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Augustus?
entries.text: Augustus (Latin: Imperator Caesar Dīvī Fīlius Augustus; 23 September 63 BC – 19 August 14 AD) was the first Roman Emperor, ruling from 27 BC until his death in AD 14. He led Rome in its transition from the Roman Republic to the Roman Empire.
entries.title: Augustus

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Archimedes?
entries.text: Archimedes of Syracuse (c. 287 – c. 212 BC) was a Greek scientist. He was an inventor, an astronomer, and a mathematician.
entries.title: Archimedes

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Leonhard Euler?
entries.text: Leonhard Euler (pronounced Leonard Oiler) (April 15, 1707 – September 7, 1783) was a Swiss mathematician and physicist. He spent most of his adult life in Russia and Germany.
entries.title: Leonhard Euler

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Dmitri Mendeleev?
entries.text: Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev (born 8 February (O.S. 27 January) 1834 near Tobolsk – 2 February (O.S. 20 January 20) 1907 in Saint Petersburg) was a Russian chemist who created the periodic table of elements.
entries.title: Dmitri Mendeleev

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was George Frideric Handel?
entries.text: George Frideric Handel (German: Georg Friedrich Händel) (23 February 1685 – 14 April 1759) was an German composer who went to live in England when he was a young man and later became a naturalised Briton. Johann Sebastian Bach and Handel were born in the same year.
entries.title: George Frideric Handel

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Akira Kurosawa?
entries.text: Akira Kurosawa (March 23, 1910 – September 6, 1998) was a Japanese movie director. Kurosawa's movies are liked in Japan.
entries.title: Akira Kurosawa

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Victor Hugo?
entries.text: Victor Marie Hugo (26 February 1802 – 22 May 1885) was a French poet, playwright, novelist, statesman and human rights activist. He played an important part in the Romantic movement in France.
entries.title: Victor Hugo

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Alexander Pushkin?
entries.text: Alexander Sergeyevich Pushkin was born 6 June (26 May, Old Style) 1799, Moscow, and died 10 February 1837 (29 January, New Style), St Petersburg. He was a Russian poet, novelist, dramatist and writer of short stories.
entries.title: Alexander Pushkin

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Beauty?
entries.text: Beauty is a property of certain things. Something is beautiful if it is nice to look at it, hear it, feel it, taste it, smell it or think about it.
entries.title: Beauty

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Imperialism?
entries.text: Imperialism is a policy (way of governing) in which large or powerful countries seek to extend their authority beyond their own borders. The policy of imperialism aims at the creation of an empire.
entries.title: Imperialism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Military?
entries.text: Military forces (often called the military when specific to a certain group) are groups of people that are given power to defend a country or territory with weapons. They are armed, so they are called the armed forces.
entries.title: Military

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Syllable?
entries.text: A syllable is a unit of pronunciation uttered without interruption, loosely, a single sound. All words are made from at least one syllable.
entries.title: Syllable

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Metre?
entries.text: The metre (British spelling) or meter (American spelling) (symbol: m) is the basic unit of length in the SI measurement system. The symbol for the metre is m.
entries.title: Metre

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Nature?
entries.text: The words nature and natural are used for all the things that are normally not made by humans. The word comes from the Latin natura meaning "birth".
entries.title: Nature

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Endangered species?
entries.text: An endangered species is a group of animals or plants which is threatened by becoming extinct. This could happen because there are few of that animal left, its predators have grown in number, or the climate that it lives in is changing, or the places it lives in have been destroyed.
entries.title: Endangered species

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Fungus?
entries.text: A fungus (plural: fungi) is a type of living organism that includes yeasts, molds, mushrooms and others. Fungi are a category of organism as large and varied as the animals or plants.
entries.title: Fungus

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Immune system?
entries.text: The immune system is the set of tissues which work together to resist infections. The immune mechanisms help an organism identify a pathogen, and neutralize its threat.
entries.title: Immune system

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Blindness?
entries.text: Blindness is to not see anything. Some people are called blind, even though they can see a little bit.
entries.title: Blindness

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Cereal?
entries.text: Cereal usually refers to a type of grass that is grown to be eaten. Some, such as wheat, are mostly used to feed people.
entries.title: Cereal

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Transistor?
entries.text: A transistor is an electronic component that can be used as part of an amplifier, or as a switch. It is made of a semiconductor material.
entries.title: Transistor

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Diode?
entries.text: A diode is an electronic component with two electrodes (connectors) that allows electricity to go through it in one direction and not the other direction.
entries.title: Diode

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Bicycle?
entries.text: A bicycle (or bike) is a small, human powered land vehicle with a seat, two wheels, two pedals, and a metal chain connected to cogs on the pedals and rear wheel. A frame gives the bike strength, and the other parts are attached to the frame.
entries.title: Bicycle

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Gunpowder?
entries.text: Gunpowder (or gun powder) is a mix of chemical substances (75% saltpeter, 15% charcoal and 10% sulfur). It is used primarily in firearms, burns very quickly, and creates gases.
entries.title: Gunpowder

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Athletics?

entries.title: Athletics (sport)

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.title: People's Republic of China

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.title: Paris

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: The Tasman Sea is the sea between Australia and New Zealand. It was named after Dutch explorer Abel Tasman.

entries.text: The Iberian Peninsula, or Iberia, is the southwest part of Europe. Like other peninsulas, it is mostly surrounded by sea.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: The modern English alphabet is a Latin alphabet of 26 letters (each having an uppercase and a lowercase form), of which five are vowels (a, e, i, o, and u) and 21 are consonants – exactly the same letters that are found in the ISO basic Latin alphabet: The exact shape of printed letters changes depending on the typeface (and font). The shape of handwritten letters can be very different from the standard printed form (and between individuals), especially when written in cursive style. See the individual letter articles for information about letter shapes and origins (follow the links on any of the uppercase letters above). Written English uses 18 digraphs (strings of two letters to represent just one sound), such as ch, sh, th, ph, wh, etc., but they are not considered separate letters of the alphabet. Some traditions also call two ligatures, æ and œ, and the ampersand (&) part of the alphabet.
entries.title: English alphabet
